# SyberLabs

> SyberLabs builds verification software for AI systems: code checks, executable docs, source-traced workspaces, and custom agent engineering.

> **RISE and AI models:** since RISE #294 the RISE server calls no model. An AI reading request runs on the reader’s own connection: hosted Jev through the reader’s OpenRouter account, or a pinned Kev-4B on the reader’s machine (`/kev/` on the site). local Kev did not meet RISE’s bar in internal checks on RISE’s evaluations (RISE `docs/product/tasks/SCR-004.json`), and there is no production Kev deployment, by design. Once the reader connects, RISE’s visual direction sends sections of the reading text to that connection.

This file is generated from the site’s own data (projects/site-data.js in github.com/SyberLabs/SyberLabs.github.io) by scripts/llms.mjs. Each project line carries a "Reflects" stamp: the repository commit and date its claims were checked against. Every project claim is taken from its repository at the commit named in `reflects` or its public page. Evidence states: implemented (the behaviour exists in code), tested (a named test exercises it), measured (numbers exist under stated conditions), deployed (it runs somewhere people can reach). Nothing is promoted from one state to the next by wording.

## When to use this file

- Use it to learn what SyberLabs is, which projects exist, what state each one has reached, and where its page, source and live app are.
- Use the "Reflects" commit as the version to read: for code-level questions, read the source repository at that commit (for example with a code index such as GitHits, where the repository is public).
- Quote the evidence lines as written. A project that is implemented or tested is not thereby deployed or measured, and "not yet" lines are part of the claim.
- Read the [full text](https://syberlabs.io/llms-full.txt) for every field each project page shows, including demo captions and run output.

## When not to use this file

- Do not treat it as newer than the Reflects stamp. If a repository has moved on, the repository is the authority for code and this file for what the site claims.
- Do not infer capabilities, users, metrics or deployments that are not stated here; the site states its limits on purpose.
- It describes a website. It is not an API, SDK or package, and it carries no credentials. Never send keys or private data to the contact address.

## Products

- [SyberWork](https://syberlabs.io/projects/syberwork/): Software factory. SyberWork is an open-source Python runtime for AI coding agents. It executes contract checks independently on every proposed diff, enforces explicit approval rules, and logs every step in a cryptographically signed chain.
  - Status: In development
  - Reflects: SyberLabs/SyberWork@208eaf6 · verified 2026-10-05
  - Source: https://github.com/SyberLabs/SyberWork
  - Evidence, tested: 23 golden conformance traces, clean-install release gate, and green CI across CPython 3.11 to 3.13.
  - Evidence, measured: Single-machine SQLite medians: explain.allowed 3.8 µs, complete_case 37.4 ms, 501-event chain verification 10.2 ms.
  - Evidence, implemented: End-to-end procurement workflow against a reference system with idempotent order POSTs and manager sign-off.
  - Evidence, not yet: Local loopback only; no external SDK adopters. Benchmark completed one three-fixture pilot that proved too simple for general conclusions.
- [Attest](https://syberlabs.io/projects/attest/): Documentation testing. Point Attest at a README, quickstart, AI how-to response, or product spec. It executes shell commands in a scratch directory and UI steps in Chrome, returning every claim marked proven, stale, broken, unverifiable, or skipped with full evidence.
  - Status: Public source · early
  - Reflects: SyberLabs/attest@274b8e7 · verified 2026-11-05
  - Source: https://github.com/SyberLabs/attest
  - Evidence, measured: At Kane CLI Hack Day (San Francisco, 24 October 2026), proved 9 documents across 23 turns with 31 screenshot-backed browser claims.
  - Evidence, measured: Caught live drift: Vite’s starter page changed from “Vite + React” to “Get started”; GitHub renamed “Security & analysis” to “Advanced Security”.
  - Evidence, tested: Unit and red-team suites covering forged approvals, protected-promise tampering, and path-escape attacks.
  - Evidence, not yet: Local CLI only, with unsandboxed shell execution and no hosted service. No external production teams yet.
- [RISE](https://syberlabs.io/projects/rise/): Browser reading app. A browser-based reading instrument. Words unfold at your pace alongside synthesized audio and procedural visuals, with instant switching to a traditional page view.
  - Status: Live · open beta
  - Reflects: SyberLabs/RISE@998d725 · verified 2026-10-05
  - Source: https://github.com/SyberLabs/RISE
  - Live: https://rise.syberlabs.io/ (No account, API key, or install required. Pick a reading and press Begin.)
  - Evidence, deployed: Reader, Library, Chapel, Make rooms, and interactive sample live at rise.syberlabs.io.
  - Evidence, tested: CI runs unit, integration, and Playwright suites, first-load budgets, and architecture checks on every release.
  - Evidence, measured: ChatGPT developer-mode test (4 October 2026) produced a validated Current and audible narration. Partial validation, not a public listing.
  - Evidence, tested: RISE Plus voice, optional ElevenLabs narration ($8.99/month): merged and verified in Stripe test mode (8 October 2026); paid launch pending verification.
  - Evidence, not yet: No external reader study or physical-device user testing conducted.
- [FLYSPACE](https://syberlabs.io/projects/flyspace/): AI data canvas. FLYSPACE (formerly OmniOS) is a visual canvas for connecting data sources to AI assistants. Every answer records and cites the exact incoming sources that produced it.
  - Status: Live preview
  - Reflects: SyberLabs/Flyspace@e95ae73 · verified 2026-10-05
  - Source: https://github.com/SyberLabs/Flyspace
  - Live: https://omni.syberlabs.io/ (Browser preview live at omni.syberlabs.io. Your canvas stays local in your browser.)
  - Evidence, deployed: Limited public preview live at omni.syberlabs.io since 3 October 2026 on Cloudflare Workers.
  - Evidence, tested: Unit suites across stores, services, and capability engine, plus 6 Playwright specs covering the full morning workflow.
  - Evidence, implemented: Capability compiler and server-side broker hardened against fixtures and stubbed transports.
  - Evidence, not yet: No third-party APIs or MCP servers measured in production. Speech tested via typed transcripts only. Identity issuer not yet provisioned.

## Research

- [Research index](https://syberlabs.io/research/): All 12 SyberLabs research artifacts: technical reports, fault-injection studies, working papers, and Lacuna provenance datasets with explicit limits.
- [Lacuna Institute](https://syberlabs.io/lacuna/): Lacuna Institute maps 21 sites where the historical record breaks down, separating verified primary sources from open questions and speculation.
- [Paracas bundles](https://syberlabs.io/lacuna/research/paracas-bundles/): Open CC BY 4.0 census of 13 Wari Kayan Paracas mummy bundles documented leaving Peru, with destinations, presumed holders, and graded sources.

## Company

- [Services](https://syberlabs.io/services/): AI consulting, custom verifiable agent systems, and developer-tool design partnerships built with automated checks, signed logs, and human sign-off.
- [PSYCHO SYBER](https://syberlabs.io/psycho-syber/): Play PSYCHO SYBER in your browser: a six-stage stealth game translating Attest, RISE, FLYSPACE, SyberWork, and Lacuna Institute into game mechanics.

## How we build

- [The Factory](https://syberlabs.io/factory/): Six-stage pipeline governing AI code changes in SyberWork: scoped context, isolated diffs, independent checks, policy review, and human sign-off.
- [Approach](https://syberlabs.io/approach/): SyberLabs' five engineering rules for verifiable AI systems: bounded action spaces, independent checks, explicit provenance, and human approval.
- [/stack/](https://syberlabs.io/stack/): How SyberLabs grounds coding agents in exact open-source dependency versions via GitHits, plus exact setup commands and data-disclosure boundaries.
